Name: Euniesses Hernandez
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Implementing "Care First, Jails Last" community safety models. 2. Expanding tenant protections and social housing initiatives. 3. Increasing green space and pedestrian safety in high-density neighborhoods.
About Me: Eunisses Hernandez is a community organizer, a daughter of Mexican immigrants, and a lifelong District 1 resident. Born and raised in Highland Park, she led campaigns, coalitions, and commissions that transformed local and statewide policy before running for City Council in 2021. Since taking office in December 2022, Councilmember Hernandez has prioritized a Care First agenda that focuses on investing in community care, workforce development, social services, and harm-reduction programs that help make our neighborhoods safer and healthier places for all Angelenos.

Name: Adrin Nazarian
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Securing state-level funding for San Fernando Valley transit projects. 2. Implementing earthquake resilience and infrastructure modernization. 3. Strengthening fiscal oversight of city departments.
About Me: Adrin Nazarian is a seasoned public servant whose journey from an eight-year-old refugee fleeing the Iran-Iraq war to a prominent Los Angeles leader defines his commitment to the San Fernando Valley. After earning an economics degree from UCLA and honing his expertise as a CORO Fellow and Chief of Staff, Nazarian served a productive decade in the California State Assembly, where he launched the nation’s largest college savings program and expanded regional transit. Now representing Council District 2, he leverages his legislative experience as Chair of the Energy and Environment Committee, focusing on the city’s infrastructure resilience following the 2025 wildfires and spearheading the "Keep Hollywood Home" campaign to protect the region's signature film and television industry.

Name: Bob Blumenfield
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Leading the "Warner Center 2035" sustainable development plan. 2. Championing "Cabin Community" interim housing for the unhoused. 3. Promoting environmental sustainability through "EV Ready" building codes.
About Me: Serving as the Chair of the Budget and Finance Committee, Blumenfield balances fiscal responsibility with a passion for environmental technology and smart urban planning.

Name: Nithya Raman
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Scaling the "Circular" homelessness outreach model citywide. 2. Eliminating parking minimums to lower housing construction costs. 3. Leading the city’s transition toward carbon-neutral building standards.
About Me: Nithya Raman is an urban planner and Los Angeles City Councilmember representing District 4, known for her work on homelessness, housing, and climate issues. A Harvard and MIT graduate, immigrant, and working mother, she previously co-led local homelessness initiatives before winning a historic 2020 election as the first Asian-American woman and first South Asian on the Council, and was re-elected in 2024. As Chair of the Housing and Homelessness Committee and a member of several key committees and regional boards, she focuses on expanding affordable housing, improving city services, and advancing climate goals, while maintaining a proactive, community-centered approach to constituent services.

Name: Katy Yaroslavksy
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Expanding the city’s recycled water infrastructure. 2. Increasing oversight of the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA). 3. Enhancing public transit connectivity on the Westside.
About Me: Katy Yaroslavsky is the Los Angeles City Councilwoman for District 5, elected in 2022, with a focus on sustainability, equity, and improving quality of life. A lifelong Angeleno, she chairs the Budget and Finance Committee, serves on several other council committees, and was appointed to the LA Metro Board in 2023. Before her election, she worked as a senior policy advisor where she advanced major environmental and infrastructure initiatives, including creating LA County’s first Office of Sustainability, helping pass Measure W, and supporting the Clean Power Alliance. Guided by a belief that issues like homelessness, climate change, and economic inequality are interconnected, she emphasizes coalition-building and community engagement; she is a UC Berkeley and UCLA Law graduate and lives in Mid City with her family.

Name: Imelda Padilla
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Revitalizing commercial corridors in the central San Fernando Valley. 2. Expanding youth development and after-school programs. 3. Improving local park safety and maintenance.
About Me: Imelda Padilla is the Los Angeles City Councilmember representing the Sixth District in the San Fernando Valley, bringing over 20 years of experience in community organizing, advocacy, and public service. A lifelong Valley resident, she has worked on initiatives supporting working families, education, environmental justice, and healthcare access, including roles with Pacoima Beautiful, the LA Alliance for a New Economy, and as a Field Deputy for her district. Now in office, she focuses on improving city services, public safety, homelessness solutions, and government transparency, while also serving on multiple council committees and as Chair of the Government Operations Committee. In 2025, she became the first Latina from the East Valley appointed to the Metro Board, and she holds degrees from UC Berkeley and Cal State Northridge.

Name: Monica Rodriguez
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Spearheading the "Clean Streets" initiative in the North Valley. 2. Championing small business recovery and entrepreneurship. 3. Investing in fire-prevention infrastructure for hillside communities.
About Me: Monica Rodriguez has served on the Los Angeles City Council since 2017, becoming the third Latina in the city’s history to do so and representing the community where she was raised. Shaped by her immigrant family background, she has focused her career on expanding opportunity and equity, particularly for underserved communities. As a councilmember, she has prioritized affordable housing, homelessness, public safety, youth opportunities, and small business support, while securing major investments for infrastructure, parks, and community programs in her district. As Chair of the Public Safety Committee, she has led initiatives on emergency response, policing, and illegal operations, and has advanced innovative homelessness solutions like safe parking sites and navigation hubs. Her broader work includes promoting economic equity, supporting women and minority-owned businesses, and fostering community development, reflecting a results-driven approach to improving quality of life in Los Angeles.

Name: Marqueece Harris-Dawson
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Leading "Destination Crenshaw," a major cultural and economic project. 2. Implementing the "United to House LA" (Measure ULA) funding. 3. Improving traffic safety through the "Western Avenue Task Force.
About Me: Marqueece Harris-Dawson, President of the Los Angeles City Council, is a longtime community activist and public servant who has represented South Los Angeles since 2015. Shaped by his early experiences growing up during the crack cocaine epidemic, he has focused on advancing social justice, affordable housing, and public safety. He co-authored Proposition HHH, a major housing initiative that significantly expanded supportive housing in his district, and has promoted community-centered policing through the Community Safety Partnership. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he launched programs to support small businesses and seniors, and he has championed creative projects like transforming a Metro site into a cultural space celebrating Black history. Known for his pragmatic and progressive leadership, he continues to lead key council committees while working to improve quality of life across Los Angeles.

Name: Curren D. Price, Jr.
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Establishing the "Basic Income Guaranteed" (BIG:LEAP) pilot program. 2. Decriminalizing street vending and supporting micro-entrepreneurs. 3. Major redevelopment of the Figueroa Corridor.
About Me: Since taking office in 2013, Los Angeles City Councilmember Curren Price has focused on improving economic opportunity, public safety, and quality of life in South Central’s District 9 through major labor, housing, and community investments. A lifelong resident of the district, he has championed landmark policies such as minimum wage increases, fair work scheduling, and “Ban the Box,” while also supporting small businesses and workforce development. He has led significant efforts to address homelessness and poverty, including launching one of the nation’s largest guaranteed income programs and expanding affordable housing and supportive services. Additionally, his tenure has brought billions in development, major park and infrastructure improvements, and expanded health, environmental, and cultural initiatives to the community.

Name: Heather Hutt
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Improving road conditions and pedestrian lighting in District 10. 2. Expanding senior services and community center accessibility. 3. Streamlining the delivery of permanent supportive housing.
About Me: Heather Hutt is the Los Angeles City Councilwoman for District 10, a lifelong Angeleno from Leimert Park and the first Black woman elected as a voting member for the district, as well as the only Black woman currently on the Council. With over 30 years of experience in activism and public service, she previously served as California State Director for U.S. Senator Kamala Harris and as a City Council Chief of Staff, advocating for healthcare equity, immigrant rights, and pandemic response efforts. As a councilmember, she prioritizes affordable housing, tenant protections, support for seniors, and services for vulnerable communities, including securing housing for thousands of formerly unhoused residents. She also focuses on environmental equity, infrastructure improvements, and enhancing public spaces, emphasizing a commitment to equity, community investment, and quality of life in her district.

Name: Traci Park
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Enforcing anti-camping ordinances (41.18) near sensitive sites. 2. Strengthening support for the LAPD and public safety response. 3. Promoting coastal conservation and beach maintenance.
About Me: Traci Park is the Los Angeles City Councilwoman for District 11, bringing a background shaped by working-class values and a 20-year career as a municipal attorney. The first in her family to attend college, she earned degrees from Johns Hopkins University and Loyola Law School and entered public office to address challenges facing the Westside. As a councilmember, she focuses on public safety, homelessness solutions, and responsive constituent services, while supporting local businesses, tourism, and workforce development. She emphasizes data-driven decision-making, environmental sustainability, and community engagement to build a safer, more resilient, and economically strong district.

Name: John Lee
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Protecting single-family zoning and neighborhood character. 2. Expanding public safety resources for the Northwest Valley. 3. Supporting local business growth through regulatory reform.
About Me: John Lee is the Los Angeles City Councilmember for District 12, first elected in 2019 and re-elected in 2020, bringing decades of local experience as a longtime resident and public servant. His leadership focuses on public safety, supporting small businesses, and improving core city services, with an emphasis on fiscal responsibility and government accountability. During crises like the Saddleridge Fire and COVID-19 pandemic, he led emergency response efforts and launched programs to support small businesses, students, renters, and residents at risk of homelessness. As chair of the Public Safety Committee, he advocates for strong resources for first responders while promoting prevention-based approaches to homelessness and working to maintain safe, thriving communities in the northwest San Fernando Valley.

Name: Hugo Soto-Martinez
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Removing the fence at Echo Park Lake and implementing community-led safety. 2. Expanding tenant legal defense funds and eviction protections. 3. Creating new protected bike lanes and "slow streets.
About Me: Hugo Soto-Martínez is a Los Angeles City Councilmember representing District 13, elected in 2022 as the first rank-and-file union organizer and currently the only renter on the Council. The son of Mexican immigrants and street vendors, his upbringing in a working-class community shaped his commitment to addressing inequality and supporting marginalized families. After starting work at 16, he became a longtime labor organizer with UNITE HERE Local 11, advocating for higher wages, healthcare, and workers’ rights. In office, he focuses on advancing tenant protections, workers’ rights, and inclusive policies—such as making Los Angeles a sanctuary city—aimed at improving conditions for working-class Angelenos.

Name: Ysabel J. Jurado
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Ending the displacement of long-term residents in Boyle Heights and DTLA. 2. Implementing community-led budgeting for district improvements. 3. Reforming the city’s land-use process to prevent corruption.
About Me: Ysabel Jurado is a Los Angeles City Councilmember and former tenants’ rights attorney, affordable housing advocate, and single mother, as well as the daughter of undocumented Filipino immigrants. Raised in Highland Park, she worked her way through college at UCLA and earned a law degree specializing in public interest and critical race studies. Her legal work focused on preventing evictions, supporting small businesses, promoting homeownership for communities of color, and advancing environmental and reparative justice. In office, she prioritizes affordable housing, homelessness solutions, economic equity, climate action, and support for local businesses.

Name: Tim McOsker
Top 3 Impacts: 1. Accelerating the greening of the Port of Los Angeles. 2. Facilitating labor-friendly development projects. 3. Improving public health outcomes for communities near industrial zones.
About Me: Tim McOsker is the Los Angeles City Councilmember for District 15, representing Harbor City, Harbor Gateway, San Pedro, Watts, and Wilmington since his election in 2022. A lifelong San Pedro resident, he brings decades of public service experience, including roles as Chief of Staff to Mayor James Hahn and CEO of AltaSea, a nonprofit focused on ocean sustainability and job creation. His priorities include expanding economic opportunity, improving environmental conditions, increasing affordable housing, addressing homelessness, and enhancing public safety and government transparency. He serves in multiple council leadership roles, including Chair of the Personnel & Hiring Committee and member of several key committees.
